title: Resetting Your Password
content: If you've forgotten your Cascade password, click 'Forgot password?' on the sign-in page and enter the email address associated with your account. We'll send a password reset link to that inbox. Open the email and click the link to choose a new password. For security reasons, the link is single-use and expires 24 hours after it's sent — if it expires before you use it, just request a new one from the sign-in page. Once your password is reset, you'll be signed out of all active sessions on other devices and will need to sign in again with your new password.

title: Setting Up Two-Factor Authentication
content: Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds a second layer of protection to your Cascade account. Go to Account Settings > Security and click 'Enable 2FA'. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app (such as Google Authenticator or Authy) and enter the six-digit code to confirm setup. Save your backup codes somewhere safe — you'll need one if you ever lose access to your authenticator app. Note that if you also use email-based password recovery, the reset link sent to your inbox will stay active for a while after it's issued, so there's no need to rush back to your email the moment you request it.

title: Understanding API Rate Limits
content: Every Cascade API key is subject to a rate limit to keep the platform fast and reliable for everyone. Currently, each key can make up to 100 requests per minute across all endpoints. If you exceed this limit, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests response along with a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before trying again. Rate limits apply per API key, not per account, so teams with multiple integrations can create separate keys to isolate traffic. Enterprise customers can request a higher limit by contacting support.

title: Generating and Managing API Keys
content: API keys let you authenticate programmatic requests to Cascade. To create one, go to Developer Settings > API Keys and click 'Generate New Key'. Give it a descriptive name so you can identify it later, and copy the secret immediately — it won't be shown again. Each key inherits the throughput allowance tied to your workspace, so if you're building a high-volume integration and start seeing frequent 429 responses, consider spreading requests across a longer window or batching calls rather than firing them all at once. You can revoke a key at any time from the same page; revoked keys stop working immediately.

title: Troubleshooting Common API Errors
content: This article covers the most frequent errors developers hit when integrating with Cascade. A 401 means your API key is missing or invalid — check that it's included in the Authorization header. A 404 usually means the resource ID in your request doesn't exist or belongs to a different workspace. A 429 means you've been sending requests too quickly; back off and retry after the interval suggested in the response headers. Most integrations that hit this error are polling more aggressively than they need to — if you're checking for updates more than once every second or two, you're a good candidate for webhooks instead of polling.

title: Billing and Subscription Plans Overview
content: Cascade offers three plans: Starter, Pro, and Enterprise. Starter is built for small teams getting started — it includes core features, community support, and 5GB of cloud storage per team. Pro adds priority support, advanced integrations, and a larger storage allowance, and is billed per active seat. Enterprise includes custom contracts, dedicated support, SSO, and elevated API throughput beyond the standard per-key limit. You can view your current plan and usage anytime under Billing > Overview, including how much of your storage allowance you've used and how many days remain in your billing cycle.

title: Upgrading or Downgrading Your Plan
content: To change your plan, go to Billing > Overview and click 'Change Plan'. Upgrades take effect immediately and you're charged a prorated amount for the rest of your billing cycle. Downgrades take effect at the start of your next billing cycle so you don't lose access to features you've already paid for. Before downgrading from Pro to Starter, double-check your current storage usage — if your team has accumulated a lot of files over time, dropping down to the smaller allowance on the entry-level plan could put you over the cap, and you'll need to free up space or archive old exports first.

title: Configuring Webhooks
content: Webhooks let Cascade notify your systems in real time when events happen, like a record being created or a workflow completing. To set one up, go to Developer Settings > Webhooks, click 'Add Endpoint', and enter the URL that should receive event payloads. Choose which event types to subscribe to and save. All new webhook endpoints are created on our current v2 delivery system, which sends signed JSON payloads and includes a signature header you can use to verify authenticity. You can test a webhook at any time using the 'Send Test Event' button before relying on it in production.

title: Webhook Event Payload Reference
content: This reference describes the structure of Cascade webhook payloads. Endpoints created under our legacy v1 system receive unsigned XML payloads with a flat structure and no retry metadata. Endpoints created under v2 receive signed JSON payloads with a consistent envelope containing an event type, timestamp, resource snapshot, and an X-Cascade-Signature header for verifying the sender. Both formats are currently supported side by side, so if you set up your integration a while ago, check which delivery format your endpoint is using before assuming your parsing logic matches what we now recommend for new integrations.

title: Integrating with Third-Party Apps
content: Cascade connects with popular tools like Slack, Zapier, and Google Sheets through our integrations marketplace. Most integrations authenticate via OAuth and sync automatically once connected. For custom integrations built before our current webhook system existed, you may still be pointed at our original webhook endpoint format from early in Cascade's history — these older connections continue to function for now, but we recommend checking your integration's documentation to confirm it's using our currently recommended delivery method, since older formats are being phased out over time.

title: Exporting Your Data
content: You can export your Cascade data at any time from the Data view. Select the records or report you want to save, then click the 'Export' button in the top toolbar. Choose a format — CSV, JSON, or PDF for reports — and Cascade will generate the file and prompt you to save it locally. Large exports are processed in the background and you'll get a notification with a download link when the file is ready. Exported files reflect the data as of the moment you clicked Export, so re-run the export if you need the most current snapshot.

title: Scheduling Automated Exports
content: Instead of manually exporting data each time, you can schedule recurring exports from Settings > Automation > Scheduled Exports. Pick a report, a frequency (daily, weekly, or monthly), and a destination — either an email address or a connected cloud storage folder. Each scheduled run uses the same generation process as clicking the export icon in the toolbar yourself, so the output format and contents will match what you'd get from a manual run. You can pause or edit a schedule at any time, and past runs are listed with links to re-download each file.

title: Managing Storage and File Limits
content: Every Cascade workspace has a storage allowance that covers uploaded files, generated exports, and attachments. On the Starter plan, this allowance is 5GB per team; Pro and Enterprise include larger allowances. You can check your current usage under Billing > Overview, where a progress bar shows how much of your allowance is used. If you're approaching your limit, you can delete old exports, compress large attachments, or upgrade your plan for more headroom. Once you hit your limit, new uploads and exports will be blocked until you free up space or upgrade.

title: Managing Team Members and Roles
content: You can invite teammates from Settings > Team > Members by entering their email and choosing a role. Owners have full control including billing. Admins can manage members and workspace settings but not billing. Anyone you invite as an Editor today can create, modify, and delete any content in the workspace — essentially everything short of billing and member management. Viewers can see content but not change it. Choose roles carefully, since Editors currently have broad, unrestricted content permissions; you can change a member's role at any time from the same page.

title: Understanding Permission Levels
content: Cascade currently has four permission levels: Owner, Admin, Editor, and Viewer. Owner and Admin can manage workspace settings and members. Editor can create, edit, and delete any content in the workspace, but cannot manage members or billing. Viewer can see content in read-only mode. Permissions are assigned per workspace, so a user can hold different roles in different workspaces if they belong to more than one. If you need someone to help create and edit content without giving them delete or publish rights, there currently isn't a role that draws that distinction — Editor is an all-or-nothing grant of content permissions.

title: Setting Up Single Sign-On (SSO)
content: SSO is available on the Enterprise plan and lets your team sign in to Cascade using your existing identity provider, such as Okta or Azure AD. To configure it, go to Settings > Security > SSO and follow the steps to enter your identity provider's metadata URL or upload its metadata file. Once SSO is enabled, you can require it for all members, which disables password-based sign-in for your workspace. Existing members will be prompted to link their account to your identity provider the next time they sign in.

title: Understanding Audit Logs
content: Audit logs give Admins and Owners a record of important actions taken in the workspace, such as sign-ins, permission changes, and content deletions. You can view the log under Settings > Security > Audit Log, and filter by member, date range, or action type. To share logs with a compliance team or external auditor, click the export icon at the top of the log to save the filtered results as a CSV file. Audit logs are retained for 90 days on Pro and indefinitely on Enterprise.

title: Canceling Your Account and Data Retention
content: If you need to cancel your Cascade subscription, go to Billing > Overview and click 'Cancel Plan'. Your workspace remains accessible in a read-only state until the end of your current billing period, after which it's deactivated. We retain your data for 30 days after deactivation in case you change your mind — reactivating during that window restores full access with everything intact. After 30 days, all workspace data, including uploaded files and past exports, is permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
